description: Engineering as graph-resident theory. The physical-world disciplines: mechanical (statics, dynamics, materials, strength, machine design), electrical (circuits, EM, power, signals, control), civil/structural (structures, soil, hydraulics), chemical (mass/energy balance, reactors, separations), aerospace (aerodynamics, propulsion, orbital), thermodynamics + heat transfer + fluid mechanics, manufacturing (machining, additive, GD&T, quality), reliability + systems engineering + engineering economics + standards. Beyond what computer_architecture + embedded covered (microelectronics + RT systems): the physical-world disciplines that determine what a machine can actually do.
category_inheritance: genlMt → compiler_theory + embedded_iot_realtime. Engineering correctness arguments map to compiler_theory equivalence vocabulary: stress < yield is referential transparency (always-safe condition); FOS calculations are cost equivalence with safety margin; reliability MTBF is denotational equivalence in the limit; failure mode analysis is algebraic law over failure tree.

concepts.name: engineering_method
concepts.definition: Define problem → research → design → analyse → prototype → test → iterate → deploy. Iterative + bounded by constraints.
concepts.why: Distinguishes engineering from science. Engineering: solve a problem within constraints. Science: understand phenomenon. Different objective; different methods.

concepts.name: factor_of_safety
concepts.definition: FOS = capacity / demand. Margin built into design above expected loads.
concepts.why: Loads + properties have uncertainty. FOS accommodates. Typical: 2-3 for ductile static, 6+ for dynamic + brittle, 8+ for human safety. Standards specify.

concepts.name: design_constraints
concepts.definition: Bounds on solution: cost, weight, performance, safety, regulation, manufacturing, time.
concepts.why: Engineering = optimisation within constraints. Constraints define feasible space. Trade-offs between conflicting constraints drive design decisions.

concepts.name: tradeoff_analysis
concepts.definition: Compare options across multiple criteria. Decision matrix, Pareto front, sensitivity analysis.
concepts.why: Multi-objective. Light + strong + cheap rarely all three. Engineer picks tradeoff. Trade studies formalise.

concepts.name: iterative_design
concepts.definition: Initial concept → analysis reveals issues → refined design → repeat. Convergent.
concepts.why: First design rarely optimal. Each iteration learns. Cost of iteration vs cost of failure determines depth. Modern: rapid prototyping accelerates.

concepts.name: statics_equilibrium
concepts.definition: Σ F = 0, Σ M = 0. Object in equilibrium has zero net force + moment.
concepts.why: Foundation of structural analysis. Solve for unknown forces/reactions. Truss + beam + frame analysis. First-year engineering content.

concepts.name: free_body_diagram
concepts.definition: Isolated body with all forces (applied, reactions, weights) shown. Foundation of statics.
concepts.why: Visualise + organise force equilibrium. Critical skill. Mistakes here propagate through whole analysis. Standard engineering practice.

concepts.name: moment_force_about_point
concepts.definition: M = r × F. Tendency of force to rotate body about point.
concepts.why: Equilibrium of moments. Beam bending. Torque. Cross product gives axis + magnitude. Universal in engineering.

concepts.name: centroid_centre_of_mass
concepts.definition: Geometric centre (centroid) + weighted geometric centre (centre of mass). For uniform density: same.
concepts.why: Beam moments + dynamics. Bending stress = M*c/I where c distance from centroid. Stability analyses.

concepts.name: moment_of_inertia_area
concepts.definition: I = ∫y² dA. Measure of cross-section's resistance to bending.
concepts.why: Bending stress σ = My/I. Higher I → less stress for same moment. I-beams + tubes have high I for their weight. Foundation of beam design.

concepts.name: moment_of_inertia_mass
concepts.definition: I_mass = ∫r² dm. Rotational inertia.
concepts.why: Newton's law for rotation: τ = Iα. Flywheels, gyroscopes, vehicle dynamics. Distinct from area moment of inertia.

concepts.name: kinematics_translation
concepts.definition: v = dx/dt, a = dv/dt. Position, velocity, acceleration relations.
concepts.why: Motion description without forces. Foundation. Integration relations: x = ∫v dt, v = ∫a dt.

concepts.name: kinematics_rotation
concepts.definition: ω = dθ/dt, α = dω/dt. Angular position, velocity, acceleration.
concepts.why: Rotating machinery, robotics, motor analysis. Linear-rotational analogy: x↔θ, v↔ω, a↔α, F↔τ, m↔I.

concepts.name: Newton_second_law
concepts.definition: F = ma. Force equals mass times acceleration.
concepts.why: Foundation of dynamics. Vector equation: per-axis. Free body diagram + Newton = solve dynamics. Modern: F = dp/dt for variable mass.

concepts.name: energy_conservation
concepts.definition: KE + PE + heat dissipated = constant. Energy not lost, only converted.
concepts.why: Alternative to F=ma. Often easier: scalar, no vector decomposition. PE = mgh, KE = ½mv², rotational KE = ½Iω².

concepts.name: work_energy_theorem
concepts.definition: Work done on object = ΔKE. W = ∫F·dx.
concepts.why: Forces along path. Conservative vs non-conservative. Foundation of energy methods.

concepts.name: impulse_momentum
concepts.definition: Impulse J = ∫F dt = Δp. Momentum p = mv.
concepts.why: Collisions, impacts, jet propulsion. Short-duration high forces analysed via impulse. Conservation: total momentum constant if no external forces.

concepts.name: stress_strain
concepts.definition: Stress σ = F/A (force per area). Strain ε = ΔL/L (deformation per length).
concepts.why: Material response. Stress causes strain. Hooke's law σ = Eε for elastic regime. Foundation of strength of materials.

concepts.name: Youngs_modulus
concepts.definition: E = σ/ε in elastic range. Material stiffness.
concepts.why: Steel: 200 GPa. Aluminum: 70 GPa. Wood: 10 GPa. Higher E = stiffer = less deflection under load. Material property.

concepts.name: yield_strength
concepts.definition: Stress at which permanent (plastic) deformation begins.
concepts.why: Design boundary: stay below yield. FOS applied. Steels: 250-2000 MPa. Aluminum: 100-500 MPa. Critical material property.

concepts.name: ultimate_tensile_strength
concepts.definition: Maximum stress before fracture. Higher than yield for ductile materials.
concepts.why: Maximum load capacity. Beyond yield: plastic deformation; beyond UTS: necking → fracture. Standard material spec.

concepts.name: ductile_vs_brittle
concepts.definition: Ductile: large plastic deformation before fracture. Brittle: little to no plastic deformation.
concepts.why: Failure mode matters. Ductile (steel, copper) warns by deforming. Brittle (cast iron, ceramics, concrete) catastrophic failure. Design philosophy differs.

concepts.name: fatigue_SN_curve
concepts.definition: Stress vs cycles-to-failure. Materials fail at lower stress under cyclic loading.
concepts.why: Most service failures are fatigue. Steel: endurance limit (~half UTS) — infinite life if below. Aluminum: no endurance limit. Critical design consideration.

concepts.name: fracture_mechanics
concepts.definition: Crack propagation under stress. Stress intensity factor K. Critical: K_IC.
concepts.why: Cracks reduce capacity beyond what cross-section suggests. Aerospace, pressure vessels, fracture-critical analysis. Damage tolerance philosophy.

concepts.name: creep
concepts.definition: Slow plastic deformation under sustained load + elevated temperature.
concepts.why: Pressure vessels, turbines, nuclear. Material gradually deforms over years. Limits service life. Tested via creep curves.

concepts.name: bending_stress_formula
concepts.definition: σ = My/I. M moment, y distance from neutral axis, I area moment of inertia.
concepts.why: Beam design fundamental. Maximum stress at extreme fibres (y_max). Drives beam shape selection.

concepts.name: shear_stress
concepts.definition: τ = V/A for direct shear. Beam shear: τ = VQ/Ib.
concepts.why: Bolts, welds, fasteners loaded in shear. Beam transverse loading creates both bending + shear. Different failure modes.

concepts.name: torsion
concepts.definition: Torque on shaft. Shear stress τ = Tr/J. J polar moment of inertia.
concepts.why: Drive shafts, axles. Hollow shaft most efficient: outer fibres do most work. Combined bending + torsion in real shafts.

concepts.name: carbon_steel
concepts.definition: Iron + 0.05-2% carbon. Higher carbon = harder + stronger + more brittle.
concepts.why: Workhorse structural material. Mild steel (A36) for structures; high carbon for tools. Cheap, recyclable, weldable.

concepts.name: alloy_steel
concepts.definition: Steel + alloying elements (Cr, Ni, Mo, V). Improved properties.
concepts.why: Stainless (Cr): corrosion resistance. Tool steel (Mo, V): hardness retention. High-strength low-alloy (HSLA): strength + weldability.

concepts.name: aluminum_alloys
concepts.definition: Series-designated: 1xxx pure, 2xxx Cu, 6xxx Mg+Si (architectural), 7xxx Zn (aerospace).
concepts.why: Strength-to-weight. Corrosion resistance via oxide layer. 7075 + 2024 aerospace. 6061 general structural. Lower stiffness than steel.

concepts.name: polymers_thermoplastics
concepts.definition: PE, PP, PVC, PET, nylon. Melt + reform. Recyclable.
concepts.why: Cheap, light, electrical insulator, corrosion-immune. Cost: low strength, creep, low temperature limit. Mass-production friendly.

concepts.name: polymers_thermosets
concepts.definition: Epoxy, polyester, polyurethane, phenolic. Irreversibly cured. Crosslinked.
concepts.why: Better thermal + chemical resistance than thermoplastics. Used as matrix in composites. Cannot be remelted.

concepts.name: composites_fiber_reinforced
concepts.definition: Fibers (glass, carbon, aramid) in matrix (polymer). Combine fiber strength + matrix load transfer.
concepts.why: Aerospace, sporting goods, automotive. CFRP: 60-70% of titanium strength at 1/4 density. Cost: expensive, anisotropic, harder to recycle.

concepts.name: ceramics_engineering
concepts.definition: Inorganic + non-metallic. Alumina, silicon carbide, zirconia.
concepts.why: Extreme temperature, hardness, wear. Engine components, cutting tools, body armor. Cost: brittle, hard to machine, expensive.

concepts.name: phase_diagram
concepts.definition: Plot of phases vs composition + temperature. Fe-C diagram famous for steel.
concepts.why: Predicts microstructure. Heat treatment uses phase changes to control properties. Foundation of metallurgy.

concepts.name: heat_treatment
concepts.definition: Controlled heating + cooling changes microstructure. Annealing, quenching, tempering, normalising.
concepts.why: Same alloy, different properties via heat treatment. Hardened tool steel vs annealed = vastly different. Critical for metal components.

concepts.name: corrosion
concepts.definition: Material degradation by chemical reaction with environment. Rust, galvanic, crevice, pitting.
concepts.why: Major service-life limiter. Mitigations: paint, plating, cathodic protection, stainless steel. Engineering economic factor.

concepts.name: gear_train
concepts.definition: Mesh gears transmit power. Ratio = N_driven / N_driving = ω_driving / ω_driven.
concepts.why: Speed/torque conversion. Multiple stages for large ratios. Spur, helical, bevel, worm. Foundation of mechanical drives.

concepts.name: bearing_selection
concepts.definition: Ball, roller, plain (sleeve), magnetic. Load capacity + speed rating.
concepts.why: Rotational support. Standard catalog parts. Life calculated via L10 (life 90% reach).

concepts.name: fasteners_threaded
concepts.definition: Bolts, screws, studs. Standard sizes (metric M-series, imperial UNC/UNF).
concepts.why: Reusable joints. Preload critical. Torque-tension relationship. ISO 898 strength grades.

concepts.name: shaft_design
concepts.definition: Combined bending + torsion + axial. Design for static + fatigue.
concepts.why: Critical machine element. Soderberg / Goodman criteria for fatigue. Keyways concentrate stress.

concepts.name: spring_design
concepts.definition: Coil springs: F = kx. Constant k = Gd⁴/(8D³N). Other types: leaf, disc, torsion.
concepts.why: Force storage, vibration isolation. Material: spring steel, music wire. Fatigue analysis critical.

concepts.name: belt_chain_drive
concepts.definition: Flexible power transmission. Belts (V, flat, timing), chains (roller).
concepts.why: Distance flexibility, vibration absorption. Belts allow slip (cheap clutch); chains no slip but heavier. Timing belts: no slip.

concepts.name: first_law_thermodynamics
concepts.definition: Energy conserved. ΔU = Q - W.
concepts.why: Foundation. Energy in - energy out = stored. Applied to engines, refrigerators, processes. Universal.

concepts.name: second_law_thermodynamics
concepts.definition: Entropy of isolated system never decreases. Heat flows from hot to cold spontaneously.
concepts.why: Direction of processes. Limits efficiency: η ≤ 1 - T_cold/T_hot (Carnot). Cannot convert heat fully to work.

concepts.name: Carnot_cycle
concepts.definition: Idealized: 2 isothermal + 2 adiabatic. Maximum efficiency between two reservoirs.
concepts.why: Upper bound on efficiency. Real engines approach but never reach. η_C = 1 - T_C/T_H. Higher hot temp = higher efficiency.

concepts.name: Rankine_cycle
concepts.definition: Steam power: pump → boiler → turbine → condenser. Most electrical generation worldwide.
concepts.why: Practical implementation. Working fluid undergoes phase change. Modern supercritical Rankine: 45%+ efficiency.

concepts.name: Brayton_cycle
concepts.definition: Gas turbine: compressor → combustor → turbine. Jet engines + power plants.
concepts.why: Aircraft propulsion + peaker plants. Open cycle (jet) vs closed. ~40% efficiency for modern combined cycle.

concepts.name: Otto_cycle
concepts.definition: Idealized spark-ignition engine: intake, compress, ignite, expand, exhaust.
concepts.why: Petrol engines. Efficiency = 1 - 1/r^(γ-1) where r compression ratio. Higher r = higher efficiency (knock limits).

concepts.name: Diesel_cycle
concepts.definition: Idealized compression-ignition. Higher compression ratio than Otto.
concepts.why: Diesel engines. Higher efficiency than Otto (~40% vs ~30%). Cost: higher peak pressures, NOx emissions.

concepts.name: refrigeration_cycle
concepts.definition: Vapor-compression: evaporator → compressor → condenser → expansion valve.
concepts.why: Refrigeration + air conditioning + heat pumps. COP = Q/W > 1 possible (moving heat, not creating). Reversed Rankine.

concepts.name: conduction_Fourier
concepts.definition: q = -k∇T. Heat flows from hot to cold proportional to temperature gradient.
concepts.why: Solid heat transfer. k thermal conductivity: Cu 400 W/mK, steel 50, wood 0.1. Insulation low k.

concepts.name: convection_Newton_cooling
concepts.definition: q = h(T_s - T_∞). Heat transfer between surface + fluid.
concepts.why: Forced (fan-cooled) vs natural (buoyancy) convection. h depends on flow + geometry. Heat exchanger design.

concepts.name: radiation_Stefan_Boltzmann
concepts.definition: q = εσT⁴. Radiative heat transfer.
concepts.why: T⁴ dominates at high T. Solar, furnaces, vacuum. Emissivity ε for surface property. Black body ε=1.

concepts.name: heat_exchanger_LMTD
concepts.definition: Log Mean Temperature Difference. q = UA·LMTD.
concepts.why: Standard heat exchanger sizing. U overall heat transfer coefficient. Parallel vs counter-flow.

concepts.name: Bernoulli_equation
concepts.definition: p + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant along streamline. Incompressible, inviscid, steady.
concepts.why: Foundation of fluid mechanics. Pressure + kinetic + potential energy. Lift, Venturi, pitot tube.

concepts.name: Reynolds_number
concepts.definition: Re = ρvD/μ. Ratio of inertial to viscous forces. Dimensionless.
concepts.why: Determines flow regime. Re < 2300 (pipe): laminar. Re > 4000: turbulent. Critical for fluid behaviour.

concepts.name: Navier_Stokes_equations
concepts.definition: ρ(∂v/∂t + v·∇v) = -∇p + μ∇²v + ρg. Momentum balance for fluid.
concepts.why: Governing equations of fluid flow. Analytical solutions rare; CFD solves numerically. Millennium Prize problem (smoothness).

concepts.name: pipe_flow_friction
concepts.definition: Darcy-Weisbach: Δp = f·(L/D)·ρv²/2. f friction factor from Moody chart.
concepts.why: Pump sizing. Friction loss + minor losses (fittings) → required pump head. Standard pipe design.

concepts.name: pump_centrifugal
concepts.definition: Impeller adds energy to fluid. Pressure rise from kinetic energy conversion.
concepts.why: Most common pump type. Pump curve: head vs flow. Operating point at intersection with system curve. Standard.

concepts.name: cavitation
concepts.definition: Vapor bubbles form when local pressure < vapor pressure. Collapse damages surfaces.
concepts.why: Pump damage, propeller erosion. NPSH (Net Positive Suction Head) prevents. Critical design consideration.

concepts.name: ohms_law
concepts.definition: V = IR. Voltage = current × resistance.
concepts.why: Foundation of circuits. Linear elements obey. Power P = VI = I²R = V²/R.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff_laws
concepts.definition: KCL: Σ I at node = 0. KVL: Σ V around loop = 0.
concepts.why: Circuit analysis. Combined with element equations (V=IR, V=L dI/dt, I=C dV/dt) solve any circuit.

concepts.name: Thevenin_equivalent
concepts.definition: Any linear two-terminal network = V_TH in series with R_TH.
concepts.why: Simplification. Replace complex network with V + R. Maximum power transfer when R_load = R_TH.

concepts.name: RC_RL_RLC_circuits
concepts.definition: Resistor + capacitor (RC), inductor (RL), or both (RLC). Time constants + resonance.
concepts.why: Filtering, transient response, oscillators. τ = RC or L/R. RLC: f₀ = 1/(2π√LC).

concepts.name: op_amp_ideal
concepts.definition: Infinite gain, infinite input impedance, zero output impedance. Inverting + non-inverting inputs.
concepts.why: Building block of analog. Negative feedback determines behavior. Buffer, amplifier, filter, integrator, summer.

concepts.name: AC_phasor_analysis
concepts.definition: Sinusoids represented as complex phasors. Impedance Z = R + jX.
concepts.why: AC circuit analysis. Frequency-domain approach. Inductor jωL, capacitor 1/(jωC). Power: real + reactive.

concepts.name: three_phase_power
concepts.definition: Three sinusoids 120° apart. Common for utility + industrial.
concepts.why: Constant power (vs single-phase pulsing), efficient transmission, simple motors. Delta + Wye configurations.

concepts.name: transformer
concepts.definition: Magnetically coupled coils. Voltage ratio = turns ratio. Power conserved (ideal).
concepts.why: Step up for transmission, down for distribution. Critical for power grid. Saturation + losses real.

concepts.name: induction_motor
concepts.definition: AC motor. Stator creates rotating field; rotor follows by induction.
concepts.why: ~80% of industrial motors. Simple, robust, no brushes. Speed ≈ synchronous speed (frequency/poles). VFDs vary speed.

concepts.name: Maxwell_equations
concepts.definition: Gauss law (∇·E = ρ/ε), no monopoles (∇·B = 0), Faraday (∇×E = -∂B/∂t), Ampere-Maxwell (∇×B = μJ + με∂E/∂t).
concepts.why: Foundation of electromagnetism. Light = EM wave. Antennas, transmission lines, RF derive from these.

concepts.name: impedance_matching
concepts.definition: Load impedance matched to source for maximum power transfer or minimum reflection.
concepts.why: RF + audio + transmission lines. Mismatch = standing waves, lost power. Smith chart for tuning. Critical for RF systems.

concepts.name: antenna_dipole
concepts.definition: Half-wave dipole: most common antenna. Length = λ/2.
concepts.why: Foundation antenna. Other types built on. Gain, radiation pattern, impedance characterised.

concepts.name: PID_controller
concepts.definition: u = Kp·e + Ki·∫e dt + Kd·de/dt. Combined error, history, prediction.
concepts.why: Most-used controller. Ziegler-Nichols + many tuning methods. Each term: present (P), past (I), future (D).

concepts.name: transfer_function
concepts.definition: G(s) = Y(s)/U(s). Output Laplace / input Laplace.
concepts.why: Linear time-invariant system representation. Poles + zeros characterise behavior. Foundation of classical control.

concepts.name: stability_root_locus
concepts.definition: Plot of closed-loop poles as gain varies. Crosses imaginary axis → unstable.
concepts.why: Graphical stability + design. Root locus rules. Standard control technique. Pre-MATLAB hand-sketched.

concepts.name: Bode_plot
concepts.definition: Magnitude + phase vs frequency. log scale. Asymptotic approximations.
concepts.why: Frequency response. Gain + phase margins for stability. Standard control + signal-processing tool.

concepts.name: state_space_representation
concepts.definition: ẋ = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du. First-order vector ODE.
concepts.why: Modern control. MIMO + nonlinear systems. Eigenvalues of A = pole locations. Controllability + observability tests.

concepts.name: model_predictive_control
concepts.definition: MPC: optimise control over receding horizon. Predict future + apply first move.
concepts.why: Constrained MIMO control. Industrial process control. Automotive, drones. Computationally expensive but powerful.

concepts.name: Fourier_transform
concepts.definition: Decompose signal into sinusoids. X(f) = ∫x(t)e^(-j2πft) dt.
concepts.why: Time ↔ frequency. Foundation of signal analysis. Filtering, spectrum analysis, communications. FFT for sampled signals.

concepts.name: Laplace_transform
concepts.definition: F(s) = ∫f(t)e^(-st) dt. Generalisation of Fourier including transients.
concepts.why: Solving linear ODEs. Transfer functions. Control system analysis. Standard tool.

concepts.name: z_transform
concepts.definition: X(z) = Σx[n]z^(-n). Discrete-time equivalent of Laplace.
concepts.why: Digital filter design + analysis. Foundation of DSP. Stability: poles inside unit circle.

concepts.name: sampling_Nyquist
concepts.definition: Sample at > 2× highest frequency to avoid aliasing.
concepts.why: Foundation of digital signal processing. Below Nyquist: aliasing distorts. Audio CD 44.1 kHz for 20 kHz signal.

concepts.name: filter_design
concepts.definition: Low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, band-stop. FIR + IIR digital.
concepts.why: Foundation of signal processing. Butterworth, Chebyshev, elliptic responses. Order vs sharpness trade.

concepts.name: truss_analysis
concepts.definition: Pin-connected members. Each in pure tension or compression. Method of joints + sections.
concepts.why: Bridges, towers, roofs. Simplifying assumption: pin joints + axial loads. Foundation of structural analysis.

concepts.name: beam_bending
concepts.definition: Distributed/point loads cause bending moment M(x). Solve via integration.
concepts.why: Building floors, vehicle frames. Beam tables for standard cases. Deflection: δ = ∫∫M/EI.

concepts.name: column_buckling
concepts.definition: Euler formula: P_cr = π²EI/(KL)². Failure mode for slender columns.
concepts.why: Long columns fail by buckling before yield. Effective length factor K depends on end conditions. Steel columns + slender struts.

concepts.name: reinforced_concrete
concepts.definition: Concrete in compression + steel in tension. Combined to handle bending.
concepts.why: Most-used structural material globally. Cheap, fire-resistant, durable. Design via ACI 318, Eurocode 2.

concepts.name: steel_structure_design
concepts.definition: AISC 360 in US. Sections from I-beam, HSS, plate, angle. LRFD + ASD methods.
concepts.why: Industrial buildings, bridges. Connections critical (bolted, welded). Higher strength than concrete; cost: corrosion + fire protection.

concepts.name: seismic_design
concepts.definition: Buildings designed for earthquake forces. Response spectrum + capacity design.
concepts.why: Life safety. Ductile detailing absorbs energy. Modern codes prescribe based on site + occupancy. ATC + Eurocode 8.

concepts.name: finite_element_method
concepts.definition: FEM: discretise domain into elements; solve PDE numerically. Foundation of CAE.
concepts.why: Complex geometries + loads. Stress, vibration, heat, fluid all FEM. ANSYS, Abaqus, COMSOL, OpenFOAM, etc.

concepts.name: machining_turning
concepts.definition: Workpiece rotates; cutting tool removes material. Lathe.
concepts.why: Cylindrical parts. Shafts, pins, bushings. Standard manufacturing process. CNC turning ubiquitous.

concepts.name: machining_milling
concepts.definition: Cutting tool rotates; workpiece on fixed table or 3-5 axis. Mill.
concepts.why: 3D parts. Pockets, slots, contours. CNC mills + machining centers. Most flexible removal process.

concepts.name: additive_manufacturing
concepts.definition: Build up layer by layer. FDM, SLA, SLS, DMLS, binder jetting.
concepts.why: Complex internal geometries impossible to machine. Topology-optimised parts. Cost: surface finish, slow, anisotropy.

concepts.name: injection_molding
concepts.definition: Polymer melted + injected into mold. Mass production.
concepts.why: Plastic parts at scale. Cheap per part; expensive tooling. Design for manufacturing: draft, uniform wall.

concepts.name: casting
concepts.definition: Molten metal poured into mold. Sand casting, die casting, investment casting.
concepts.why: Complex shapes. Foundation of metal parts before machining. Engine blocks, valve bodies, jewelry.

concepts.name: forging
concepts.definition: Hot or cold deformation of metal. Improved grain structure → strength.
concepts.why: Critical-strength parts: connecting rods, crankshafts, aerospace components. Stronger than equivalent cast.

concepts.name: welding
concepts.definition: Fusion (arc, MIG, TIG, laser) or solid-state (friction, ultrasonic).
concepts.why: Permanent joining. Stress concentrations at welds; HAZ properties changed. NDT inspection (UT, RT).

concepts.name: GD_T
concepts.definition: Geometric Dimensioning + Tolerancing. ASME Y14.5. Form, orientation, position, runout tolerances.
concepts.why: Communicate functional requirements + manufacturing variation. Bonus tolerance, MMC/LMC. Modern engineering standard.

concepts.name: six_sigma
concepts.definition: Quality methodology. 6 standard deviations between mean and spec limits = 3.4 defects per million.
concepts.why: Variation reduction. DMAIC: Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control. Adopted broadly beyond manufacturing.

concepts.name: statistical_process_control
concepts.definition: SPC: control charts monitor process. Detect special-cause variation.
concepts.why: Real-time quality. Stay within control limits = process under control. Standard in mass production.

concepts.name: Reynolds_transport_theorem
concepts.definition: System ↔ control volume conservation. Foundation of fluid mechanics + thermodynamics.
concepts.why: Mass, momentum, energy balances on flowing systems. Bridge from solid mechanics to fluid mechanics formulation.

concepts.name: mass_energy_balance
concepts.definition: Σ in - Σ out = Σ accumulated. Per species or total.
concepts.why: Foundation of process engineering. Reactor design, distillation, heat exchangers. Steady vs transient.

concepts.name: reactor_CSTR_PFR
concepts.definition: CSTR: continuous stirred tank, perfect mixing. PFR: plug flow, no mixing axially.
concepts.why: Two limiting cases for chemical reactors. Real reactors between. Different conversion + selectivity characteristics.

concepts.name: distillation
concepts.definition: Separate liquids by boiling point difference. Trays + reflux.
concepts.why: Workhorse separation. Oil refining, chemicals, alcohol. Energy-intensive — heat for vaporisation.

concepts.name: aerodynamics_lift_drag
concepts.definition: L = ½ρv²SCL, D = ½ρv²SCD. CL + CD depend on shape + angle of attack.
concepts.why: Aircraft, wind turbines, sails. Foundation of flight. Lift-to-drag ratio key efficiency measure.

concepts.name: Mach_number
concepts.definition: M = v/a. Ratio of speed to speed of sound.
concepts.why: Subsonic (M<1), transonic, supersonic (M>1), hypersonic (M>5). Shock waves form at M=1. Different aerodynamic regimes.

concepts.name: rocket_equation
concepts.definition: Tsiolkovsky: Δv = v_e × ln(m_0/m_f). Velocity change = exhaust velocity × log of mass ratio.
concepts.why: Foundation of rocketry. Exponential cost of high Δv = staging needed for orbit. Limits human spaceflight.

concepts.name: orbital_mechanics_Kepler
concepts.definition: Kepler's laws: elliptical orbits, equal areas, T² ∝ a³.
concepts.why: Satellite + interplanetary trajectory design. Foundation of astrodynamics. Hohmann transfer, gravity assist.

concepts.name: MTBF_reliability
concepts.definition: Mean Time Between Failures. Statistical measure of reliability.
concepts.why: Component selection, spare part planning. Series vs parallel reliability rules. Bathtub curve characterizes life.

concepts.name: Weibull_distribution
concepts.definition: Flexible distribution for time-to-failure. Shape + scale parameters.
concepts.why: Different shape parameters model wear-out, random, infant mortality. Standard for reliability analysis.

concepts.name: redundancy_design
concepts.definition: Parallel critical components. Reliability R_parallel = 1-(1-R)^n.
concepts.why: Increased reliability at cost of weight + cost. Critical aerospace systems. Fault tree analysis quantifies.

concepts.name: FMEA_engineering
concepts.definition: Failure Mode + Effects Analysis. Already in embedded; here as engineering-wide practice.
concepts.why: Systematic. Every component, every failure mode, every effect. RPN = Severity × Occurrence × Detection.

concepts.name: systems_engineering_V_model
concepts.definition: Requirements → architecture → design → implementation (left). Test → integration → verification → validation (right).
concepts.why: Standard for complex systems. INCOSE handbook. Drives V&V planning. Used in aerospace, defense, medical.

concepts.name: requirements_engineering
concepts.definition: Elicit + analyse + specify + validate requirements. Functional + non-functional + constraints.
concepts.why: Wrong requirements = wrong product. Foundation of systems engineering. Traceability through development.

concepts.name: trade_study
concepts.definition: Compare alternative architectures. Weighted criteria, Pareto analysis.
concepts.why: Design decisions documented. Multi-criteria. Standard at major decision points.

concepts.name: lifecycle_cost
concepts.definition: Acquisition + operations + maintenance + disposal. Often dominated by ops + maintenance.
concepts.why: Total ownership cost vs purchase price. Influences design decisions: durability, energy efficiency, repairability.

concepts.name: engineering_economics_NPV
concepts.definition: Net Present Value. Σ CF_t / (1+r)^t. Discount future cash flows to present.
concepts.why: Investment decisions. Positive NPV → accept. Foundation of project finance. Hurdle rate r.

concepts.name: engineering_economics_IRR
concepts.definition: Internal Rate of Return. Discount rate making NPV = 0.
concepts.why: Project return metric. Compare with cost of capital. Multiple IRR pitfall for non-conventional cash flows.

concepts.name: payback_period
concepts.definition: Time to recover initial investment from cash flows.
concepts.why: Simple metric. Ignores time value + post-payback. Good for short-term risk decisions; NPV better for long.

concepts.name: ASME_codes
concepts.definition: American Society of Mechanical Engineers. Pressure vessels (Section VIII), piping (B31), boilers.
concepts.why: Legal codes for pressure systems in US + many countries. Calculations + welding + NDT specified.

concepts.name: ISO_standards
concepts.definition: International Organization for Standardization. ISO 9001 (quality), 14001 (environmental), GD&T (1101).
concepts.why: Global standards. Trade + interoperability. Many countries adopt directly.

concepts.name: IEEE_standards
concepts.definition: Institute of Electrical + Electronics Engineers. IEEE 802 (networking), 1149 (JTAG), 1588 (PTP).
concepts.why: Electronics, computing, communications standards. Industry-driven, broadly adopted.

concepts.name: ASTM_materials
concepts.definition: ASTM International. Material specs (A36 steel, A572, B221 aluminum), test methods (E8 tensile).
concepts.why: Material specifications. Test methods for properties. Foundation of mechanical engineering material selection.

concepts.name: CAD_parametric
concepts.definition: Computer-Aided Design. Parametric: features + constraints; relations preserved on edit.
concepts.why: SolidWorks, Inventor, NX, Catia. Industry standard for mechanical design. 3D models drive everything.

concepts.name: FEA_workflow
concepts.definition: Geometry → mesh → boundary conditions → solver → post-process.
concepts.why: Standard CAE process. Mesh quality drives accuracy. ANSYS, Abaqus, COMSOL. Hand calculation validates.

concepts.name: CFD_workflow
concepts.definition: Geometry → mesh → BCs → turbulence model → solver. Iterative convergence.
concepts.why: Aerodynamics, HVAC, internal flow. OpenFOAM, ANSYS Fluent, STAR-CCM+. Standard for fluid analysis.

concepts.name: CAM_toolpaths
concepts.definition: Computer-Aided Manufacturing. CAD geometry → G-code for CNC.
concepts.why: Bridges design to manufacturing. Mastercam, Fusion 360, NX CAM. Drives modern manufacturing.

rules.name: factor_of_safety_accommodates_uncertainty
then: FOS provides margin above expected
rules.why: Real materials vary; real loads vary. FOS multiplies for safe design. Standard codes specify minimum FOS per application type.

rules.name: design_constrained_by_multiple_criteria
if: design must satisfy cost + weight + performance + safety + manufacturability
then: optimisation is multi-objective with Pareto trade-offs
rules.why: Single-objective: solvable. Multi: no unique optimum. Pareto front: improving one criterion degrades another. Standard engineering reality.

rules.name: Carnot_efficiency_ceiling
if: heat engine operates between T_hot and T_cold
then: efficiency ≤ 1 - T_cold/T_hot
rules.why: Second law of thermodynamics. Higher hot temp + lower cold temp = higher max efficiency. Real engines well below Carnot. Drives turbine inlet temps higher each generation.

rules.name: stress_must_stay_below_yield
then: stress / FOS < yield strength
rules.why: Yield = permanent deformation. Below yield: elastic, recovers. Above: plastic + likely failure. FOS handles uncertainty. Foundation of strength design.

rules.name: fatigue_dominates_cyclic_loading
then: fatigue strength (lower than static yield) governs
rules.why: Cyclic loads cause crack initiation + propagation. Steel endurance limit ~half UTS. Most service failures fatigue. Critical for rotating + vibrating parts.

rules.name: buckling_governs_slender_columns
if: column has high slenderness ratio (KL/r > ~100 for steel)
then: buckling occurs before yield
rules.why: Euler buckling: P_cr = π²EI/(KL)². At high KL: very low P_cr. Compression members must be designed for buckling, not yield.

rules.name: Reynolds_number_determines_flow_regime
then: Re < 2300 laminar, Re > 4000 turbulent
rules.why: Different physics: laminar smooth + low friction; turbulent chaotic + higher friction. Transition complex. Most engineering pipe flow turbulent.

rules.name: Bernoulli_neglects_viscosity_unsteady
then: valid only for inviscid + incompressible + steady flow
rules.why: Real flows have viscosity + may compress + be unsteady. Bernoulli is starting approximation. Modified forms add corrections.

rules.name: Kirchhoff_laws_complete_for_lumped_circuits
if: circuit has lumped elements + frequencies are low
then: KVL + KCL fully describe behavior
rules.why: Lumped: dimensions << wavelength. At RF: distributed parameter effects (transmission lines). KVL + KCL fundamental for DC + low-frequency AC.

rules.name: impedance_matching_max_power
if: source impedance Z_s drives load Z_L
then: maximum power transfer when Z_L = Z_s* (conjugate)
rules.why: Matched: half power dissipated in source, half in load. Critical for RF amplifiers, audio. Mismatch: reflected power, standing waves.

rules.name: PID_tuning_balances_response
then: fast response (high Kp), low steady-state error (high Ki), low overshoot (high Kd) tradeoff
rules.why: Ziegler-Nichols, Cohen-Coon methods. Increase Kp until oscillation; back off. Ki removes steady-state error; too much = oscillation. Kd anticipates; noise amplifier.

rules.name: Nyquist_sampling_required
then: sample rate must exceed 2× highest frequency
rules.why: Below: aliasing folds high-freq components into low. Above: signal perfectly recoverable. Foundation of digital signal processing.

rules.name: Maxwell_equations_universal_for_EM
then: Maxwell's equations apply (with material constitutive relations)
rules.why: Foundation. Static, quasi-static, full-wave all subsets. From circuits to antennas to optics. Quantum corrections at small scale.

rules.name: second_law_directionality
then: entropy never decreases
rules.why: Direction of spontaneous processes. Heat hot → cold. Limits efficiency. Foundation of thermodynamics. Statistical interpretation in stat mech.

rules.name: additive_manufacturing_enables_topology_optimisation
if: part complexity drives weight or cost
then: additive manufacturing enables shapes impossible to machine
rules.why: Internal lattices, organic shapes from topology optimisation. SpaceX Merlin engine parts, GE LEAP nozzle. Trade: cost, surface finish, slow.

rules.name: FEM_accuracy_depends_on_mesh
then: mesh quality + density determine accuracy
rules.why: Coarse mesh: missed stress concentrations, wrong modes. Fine mesh: accurate but expensive. Mesh refinement studies confirm convergence.

rules.name: GD_T_communicates_function_to_manufacturing
then: GD&T expresses tolerances tied to function
rules.why: ± tolerances don't capture functional needs. GD&T: position relative to datum, profile, runout. Standard since 1994 (ASME Y14.5). Drives modern manufacturing.

rules.name: MTBF_assumes_random_failures
if: component is past infant mortality + before wear-out
then: constant failure rate λ applies; MTBF = 1/λ
rules.why: Bathtub curve middle: random failures from rare events. Beginning + end have different statistics. Weibull captures all phases.

rules.name: redundancy_increases_reliability
if: n redundant components each with reliability R
then: system reliability = 1-(1-R)^n
rules.why: Parallel: failure requires all to fail. R=0.9, n=3: 0.999 system. Cost: weight + cost. Aerospace: triple redundancy standard.

rules.name: lifecycle_cost_dominates_purchase
then: operations + maintenance dominate total cost
rules.why: Power plant: 30+ years. Aircraft: decades. Fuel + maintenance >> purchase. Drives efficiency design, repairability. Standard procurement analysis.

rules.name: NPV_for_investment_decision
if: project has cash flows over time
then: NPV at hurdle rate determines accept/reject
rules.why: Time value of money. Money now > same money future. NPV > 0: accept; NPV < 0: reject. Foundation of capital budgeting.

rules.name: codes_govern_engineering_practice
if: design is for regulated sector (pressure vessels, buildings, etc.)
then: applicable codes determine acceptable practice
rules.why: ASME, ACI, AISC, NFPA, etc. Legal requirements. Engineer's licence depends on following. Codes evolve with experience + research.

rules.name: engineering_iterates_to_convergence
then: iteration with analysis converges to working design
rules.why: First design rarely optimal. Each iteration: analyse, identify weak point, modify, re-analyse. Modern CAE accelerates. Cost of iteration vs failure determines depth.
